diameterInterpretation: Approximate scale from a single-band thermal diameter of 5.55 km, with at least 20% uncertainty (1.11 km).

calibration.uncertaintyMeaning: Derived minimum 20% diameter error prescribed by the source publication for its assumed-beaming fits; not an individually estimated statistical error.
calibration.systematicMeaning: At least 20% total relative diameter uncertainty under the fixed-beaming fit; further shape/aspect effects can remain.
calibration.quantity: NEATM effective spherical diameter from W2 data with assumed beaming 1.20
calibration.selectionReason: Direct published WISE Mars-crosser fit supplies scale absent from the main NEOWISE V2 compiled catalog and current SBDB. Source-prescribed uncertainty is retained.
calibration.formula: scaleKmPerSourceUnit = diameterKm / cbrt(6 * signedSourceVolume / pi); meterScale =1000*scaleKmPerSourceUnit. Original shape coordinates are preserved.
limitations: The thermal effective spherical diameter is used as an approximate volume-equivalent display scale; no joint shape/thermal inversion or independently measured volume is implied.
The 5.55 km W2-only diameter has an assumed beaming parameter and at least 20% uncertainty; the exceptionally slow spin makes full rotation coverage especially incomplete.
calibration.visibleDescription: Approximate scale from a single-band thermal diameter of 5.55 km, with at least 20% uncertainty (1.11 km).

modelLimitations: The convex inversion resolves the broad shape; craters and concavities are unresolved. The selected pole is one of the published alternatives.
